directAnswer: Check the cooler's connections and ensure it's properly seated on the CPU. Monitor temperatures using software to identify if overheating occurs.
summary: Troubleshooting a CPU cooler involves checking physical connections, ensuring proper seating, and monitoring system temperatures.

sections.heading: Check the Connections
sections.body: Ensure that the CPU cooler's power connector is securely attached to the motherboard. Verify that any fan headers are connected properly.

sections.heading: Inspect Cooler Seating and Thermal Paste
sections.body: Remove the cooler and check for even contact with the CPU. Reapply thermal paste if necessary, ensuring it's a thin, even layer.

sections.heading: Monitor CPU Temperatures
sections.body: Use software like HWMonitor or Core Temp to check CPU temperatures. If temperatures exceed 80°C under load, further investigation is needed.

steps.title: Power Off and Unplug
steps.detail: Turn off your PC and unplug it from the power source before inspecting the cooler.

steps.title: Check Power Connection
steps.detail: Locate the CPU fan power connector on the motherboard and ensure it's firmly connected.

steps.title: Inspect Cooler Installation
steps.detail: Remove the cooler and check for proper installation and thermal paste application.

steps.title: Test with Monitoring Software
steps.detail: Boot the system and use monitoring software to check CPU temperatures under load.

faqs.question: What should I do if the cooler fan isn't spinning?
faqs.answer: Check the power connection to the fan and ensure that the fan is not obstructed by dust or debris.

faqs.question: How do I know if my CPU is overheating?
faqs.answer: If your CPU temperatures exceed 80°C during heavy usage, it may be overheating. Monitor temperatures using software tools.

faqs.question: Can I use too much thermal paste?
faqs.answer: Yes, using too much thermal paste can lead to poor heat transfer and overheating. A pea-sized amount is usually sufficient.

caveats: Different CPU coolers may have specific installation requirements. Refer to the manufacturer's manual for guidance.
Ensure your system is powered off before performing any hardware checks to avoid damage.
